The dashboard has no entities to scope to, so no context rail renders and the view takes the full width — the rail appears on nouns that own a list (see 1b). Status line at the bottom carries the mode, exactly as the TUI does.

5Events: notable moments on the timeline, and the balances you expect at them
5aEvents (g e, in LEDGER between Documents and Notifications). A notable moment on the ledger's timeline — a pay rise, a car accident, a wedding — or a balance check: on this date I expect this account to hold this much. Occasions can span dates and carry a spend target; milestones and incidents are a single day. Each event links the transactions and documents that belong to it, by tag or by hand. A balance check that disagrees with the ledger shows ⚑ in red until it's resolved. Events also show inline in Transactions (3c).

Items link to the purchase transaction; a purchase can be turned into an item from Transactions.

11Net worth · Investments: value vs contributions, allocation, holdings, trades & lots
11aInvestments (g i). The title is the portfolio switcher (i), like Loans and Credit cards. The chart separates what you put in (grey) from what it's worth (ink line); the red rule is today's unrealised gain. Allocation compares each asset class with its target and flags drift beyond ±2%. Holdings are units with a price; prices are dated so stale values are obvious. Losses are red, gains ink.

12Bills: Bill Plan vs Bill Schedule + History, pay direct or link a transaction, skip
12aBill Schedule (default tab) — per docs/bills.md, a Bill Plan is a recurring definition; the Schedule is the generated, dated rows against it, one per period. Status (Upcoming / Due / Overdue / Paid / Skipped) is derived from today's date, never stored. A ⚑ marks anything feeding Needs Attention: every Overdue row, plus any Due row inside its Bill's own Attention Lead. Past Paid and Skipped rows stay in the same table — it doubles as the Bill History, filterable by status, bill, category/account and range.

13Budgets: Progress vs Plan vs History, known costs from Bills, edit / fill / stop
13aBudget Progress (default tab) — one row per budgeted category for the current period, rolled up under parents like 18a. The bar stacks spent (solid) and known costs (hatched: unpaid Due/Overdue Schedule rows from 12a) against the budget, with a tick at period-elapsed so pace reads at a glance. LEFT = budget − spent − known costs. Unbudgeted spending is listed, never hidden.

14Budgets v2: multiple budgets, switcher, four methods — envelope, limits, split, project
14aEnvelope budget (YNAB-style zero-based). Income into on-budget accounts lands in Ready to Assign; each category gets an assigned amount, and Available = carried in + assigned + activity, rolling forward every month. Targets show what's still needed. Selecting an overspent envelope opens the inspector to cover it from Ready to Assign or another envelope. Card spending moves money into the card's payment envelope. The title is the budget switcher.

METHOD
EnvelopeZERO-BASED
Assign every dollar received to a category. Unspent money rolls forward; overspending is covered by moving money.
Category limitsCAPS
A monthly cap per category, tracked against spend. Income isn't assigned — the 13a behaviour.
Percentage split50/30/20
Group categories into buckets and aim for a share of income received each month.
ProjectONE-OFF
One total over a date range, tracked by tag or category — a renovation, a trip.
ACCOUNTS ON BUDGET
✓ Everyday✓ Bills✓ Savings✓ Offset✓ Visa PlatinumShare portfolioHome loan
Income into these accounts becomes Ready to Assign. Off-budget accounts still count toward net worth.
START FROM

BUDGETS ARE VIEWSA transaction counts in every budget that covers its account and category. Budgets never copy or own transactions, so any number can run side by side.
SWITCHINGb or the title opens the switcher from any Budgets tab. The last budget opened is remembered; the default is used on first launch and by Dashboard and 15d.

A check is a historical record, so older passing checks stay listed as an audit trail. Variances are shown in each check's own Unit and never summed. explain opens 15h.

ANZ Everyday — balance check, 31 Aug 2026
ASSERTED5,104.86
COMPUTED5,147.36
VARIANCE−42.50
The previous check on 31 Jul matched exactly, so the gap is within the 38 transactions dated 1–31 Aug. The ledger is 42.50 higher than the statement — something is counted that the bank hasn't cleared, or a debit is missing.
LIKELY CAUSES · MOST LIKELY FIRST3 OF 38
◐
29 AugUber EatsPending−42.50
Exact match — pending on the check date, so it counts in the ledger but not on the statement.
○
30 AugWoolworthsUnreconciled−61.80
Posted a day before the statement cut-off; check the date.
○
27 AugTransfer to JointUnreconciled−200.00
Also appears on Joint — confirm it isn't a duplicate.
Nothing changes until you act. Fixing the cause (clearing, re-dating or removing a transaction) re-computes the variance live. If there's no cause to find, an adjustment transaction settles it — categorised Balance adjustment, so it stays visible in reports rather than hiding the gap.
